intent.raw_query: Tokyo city break, $3000 for couple, food and tech culture, April 2026 from SFO

experiences.name: Tsukiji Outer Market Food Tour
experiences.description: Explore the bustling Tsukiji Outer Market, sampling fresh sushi, tamagoyaki, and street snacks from legendary vendors. Interact with local fishmongers and food artisans who have operated for generations, giving you an authentic taste of Tokyo's deep culinary heritage.

experiences.name: Akihabara Tech and Anime District Exploration
experiences.description: Dive into Tokyo's iconic electric town, visiting multi-floor electronics shops, retro gaming arcades, robot cafes, and cutting-edge gadget stores. Experience the epicenter of Japan's otaku and tech culture, including hands-on demos at stores like Yodobashi Camera and indie maker shops.

experiences.name: Senso-ji Temple and Asakusa Cultural Walk
experiences.description: Visit Tokyo's oldest and most iconic Buddhist temple, Senso-ji, strolling through the Nakamise shopping street lined with traditional crafts and snacks. Witness morning prayers, explore the five-story pagoda, and soak in the Edo-period atmosphere of the surrounding Asakusa district.

experiences.name: Ramen Alley Tasting Experience in Shinjuku
experiences.description: Navigate the narrow, atmospheric lanes of Shinjuku's Omoide Yokocho (Memory Lane) and nearby ramen shops, tasting regional ramen styles from tonkotsu to shoyu. Join a guided or self-directed tasting crawl through some of Tokyo's most celebrated noodle establishments, chatting with chefs about their craft.

experiences.name: teamLab Borderless Digital Art Museum
experiences.description: Immerse yourself in the world-renowned teamLab Borderless, a borderless digital art world where interactive, technology-driven installations blur the line between art and viewer. This experience perfectly merges Tokyo's tech innovation with cultural expression, offering a surreal and unforgettable multi-sensory journey.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Tokyo, Japan
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at airport at 13:00 — clear immigration, collect luggage, and take the budget-friendly Narita Express or Limousine Bus to central Tokyo. Head to your Tsukiji accommodation and check in.
day_by_day.afternoon: Once settled, take a short walk to explore the Tsukiji Outer Market. Browse the fresh seafood stalls, street food vendors, and local shops. Try tamagoyaki (Japanese rolled omelette) from a street stall and soak in the lively market atmosphere.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll along the Sumida River waterfront near Tsukiji for a relaxing evening walk. Visit the nearby Hamarikyu Gardens (free after 17:00 closing — enjoy the outer paths) and watch the city lights reflect on the water.

meals.breakfast: Eat on the plane or grab a quick onigiri (rice ball) from a 7-Eleven or FamilyMart convenience store at the airport for around ¥150
meals.lunch: Tsukiji Outer Market street food — fresh sushi set or grilled scallops for around ¥800–¥1,200
meals.dinner: Yoshinoya or Sukiya gyudon (beef bowl) near Tsukiji for around ¥500–¥700

day_by_day.notes: Get a Suica or Pasmo IC card at the airport for seamless budget travel on trains and buses throughout the trip. Exchange some yen at the airport for the best rates.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Tsukiji Outer Market early (by 7:00–8:00 AM) for the freshest experience — enjoy a breakfast of fresh tuna sashimi, tamagoyaki, and miso soup from the market stalls. Explore the dozens of specialty food shops selling dried seafood, pickles, and kitchenware.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk or take a short subway ride to Ginza. Window-shop the luxury district for free, then head to the free observation floors at the Itoya stationery flagship store (a tech-meets-culture must-see). Visit the free Ginza Six rooftop garden for city views.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Shiodome and Shimbashi area — explore the retro Shimbashi SL Plaza (old steam locomotive display) and the salaryman bar culture. Grab dinner at one of the many standing ramen or izakaya spots.

meals.breakfast: Tsukiji Outer Market fresh sushi breakfast set for around ¥1,000–¥1,500
meals.lunch: Convenience store bento from 7-Eleven or Lawson near Ginza for around ¥500–¥700
meals.dinner: Standing ramen at Fuunji-style shop in Shimbashi for around ¥800–¥1,000

day_by_day.notes: Ginza is expensive to shop but completely free to explore. Many galleries and showrooms in Ginza offer free entry — check out Sony Park or any rotating art exhibitions.

day_by_day.morning: Take the subway to Asakusa — Tokyo's most traditional district. Visit Senso-ji Temple (free entry), walk through Nakamise Shopping Street for affordable souvenirs like ningyo-yaki cakes and fans. Arrive early to avoid crowds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the backstreets of Asakusa — visit Hoppy Street for a taste of old Tokyo shitamachi culture. Walk to the nearby Kappabashi Kitchenware Street (free to browse) — a paradise for food culture enthusiasts with realistic plastic food displays and professional kitchen tools.
day_by_day.evening: Take the Tobu Skytree Line one stop to Tokyo Skytree area. Enjoy the free ground-level Solamachi shopping complex and the outdoor plaza view of the tower lit up at night. Grab street food from the Solamachi food hall.

meals.breakfast: Melon pan (sweet bread) and canned coffee from a Asakusa bakery stall for around ¥300
meals.lunch: Tempura donburi (tendon) at Daikokuya Tempura in Asakusa for around ¥1,500 — a local institution
meals.dinner: Monjayaki (Tokyo's local savory pancake) at a budget restaurant in Asakusa for around ¥1,000–¥1,500

day_by_day.notes: Senso-ji is free and stunning — the Kaminarimon gate and five-story pagoda are iconic photo spots. April may offer beautiful cherry blossom remnants in the temple grounds.

day_by_day.morning: Take the train to Akihabara — Tokyo's legendary Electric Town and tech/anime culture hub. Explore the multi-floor electronics stores like Yodobashi Camera and BIC Camera (free to browse). Visit retro game shops and manga stores on the side streets.
day_by_day.afternoon: Dive deeper into Akihabara's tech culture — visit the free floors of Radio Kaikan building for figures and collectibles. Explore the maid cafe street (window browse for free). Check out Super Potato retro game shop for vintage gaming nostalgia.
day_by_day.evening: Walk or take a short train ride to Ueno. Stroll through Ueno Park in the evening — the park is free and beautifully lit. Browse the Ameyoko Market (open until around 19:00) for cheap snacks, street food, and bargain goods.

meals.breakfast: Convenience store breakfast — onigiri + coffee for around ¥300–¥400
meals.lunch: Curry rice at a budget CoCo Ichibanya in Akihabara for around ¥700–¥900
meals.dinner: Yakitori skewers and draft beer at a standing bar under the Ueno train tracks for around ¥1,000–¥1,500

day_by_day.notes: Akihabara is best on weekends when the main street partially closes to traffic (check seasonal schedules). Bring cash — many smaller retro shops are cash-only.

day_by_day.morning: Take the train to Harajuku — visit Meiji Shrine (free entry, ¥500 for inner garden) in the morning when it's peaceful. Walk through the forested shrine grounds and observe traditional Shinto culture and architecture.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk down Takeshita Street for free people-watching and Tokyo's unique youth fashion culture. Then head to Omotesando — Tokyo's design boulevard. Browse the free architecture (Prada building, Omotesando Hills exterior) and pop into free concept stores.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Shibuya — experience the famous Shibuya Scramble Crossing at peak evening hours. Visit the free Shibuya Sky observation deck entrance area or enjoy the crossing view from the free Mag's Park terrace at Shibuya 109-2 building.

meals.breakfast: Morning set (toast, egg, coffee) at a Doutor Coffee shop for around ¥400–¥500
meals.lunch: Crepes from a Harajuku street stall for around ¥600–¥800
meals.dinner: Ramen at Ichiran or Fuumin in Shibuya — solo dining booth experience for around ¥900–¥1,100

day_by_day.notes: Sunday at Meiji Shrine may feature traditional wedding processions — a wonderful free cultural experience. Shibuya Scramble is most dramatic between 18:00–21:00.

day_by_day.morning: Take the train to Shinjuku — visit the free Tokyo Metropolitan Government Building observation decks (opens 9:30 AM) for panoramic city views including Mt. Fuji on clear days. This is one of the best free viewpoints in Tokyo.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Shinjuku Gyoen National Garden (¥500 entry) — a stunning blend of Japanese, French, and English garden styles. In late April, you may still catch late-blooming cherry blossoms or early spring flowers. Spend 2–3 hours relaxing here.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the neon-lit streets of Kabukicho (Tokyo's entertainment district) — free to walk through. Visit the Golden Gai area — a maze of tiny atmospheric bars. Have a drink at one of the tiny Golden Gai bars (cover charge around ¥500–¥1,000).

meals.breakfast: Convenience store breakfast near Tsukiji for around ¥300–¥400
meals.lunch: Katsu curry at a Shinjuku basement restaurant food court for around ¥800–¥1,000
meals.dinner: Omoide Yokocho (Memory Lane) — tiny yakitori stalls under the tracks near Shinjuku Station West Exit for around ¥1,500–¥2,000 including drinks

day_by_day.notes: Tokyo Metropolitan Government Building has both North and South towers — both free. The South tower stays open until 23:00 on most days (check schedule). Golden Gai bars are tiny and atmospheric — perfect for solo travelers.

day_by_day.morning: Take a day trip to Odaiba — Tokyo's futuristic artificial island. Take the free Yurikamome monorail view (pay ¥330 fare but the views are spectacular) or the Rinkai Line. Visit teamLab Borderless digital art museum — book tickets in advance (¥3,200) for the immersive tech-art experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Odaiba's free attractions — Odaiba Seaside Park (great views of Rainbow Bridge and the miniature Statue of Liberty), DiverCity Tokyo Plaza (free to enter, see the life-size Gundam statue outside), and the retro Palette Town area.
day_by_day.evening: Return to central Tokyo via Rainbow Bridge. Head to Hamarikyu Gardens (¥300 entry, closes 17:00) for a traditional Japanese garden experience near your hotel. End the evening with a walk along the Tsukiji waterfront.

meals.breakfast: Tsukiji Outer Market breakfast — fresh oysters and grilled fish for around ¥800–¥1,000
meals.lunch: Food court meal at DiverCity Tokyo Plaza for around ¥700–¥900
meals.dinner: Sushi conveyor belt (kaiten sushi) at Sushiro or Kura Sushi near Tsukiji for around ¥1,000–¥1,500

day_by_day.notes: TeamLab Borderless is one of Tokyo's most unique tech-culture experiences — book tickets online in advance as they sell out. Wear comfortable shoes as you'll walk a lot on Odaiba.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Yanaka — one of Tokyo's best-preserved old shitamachi (downtown) neighborhoods. Walk through Yanaka Cemetery (free, beautiful in spring) and explore the narrow lanes lined with traditional wooden houses, local craft shops, and family-run temples.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue through the Yanaka Ginza shopping street — a retro covered shopping arcade with local food stalls, tofu shops, and small restaurants. Walk to nearby Nezu Shrine (free entry) — a smaller but beautiful alternative to Fushimi Inari with hundreds of torii gates.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Akihabara (nearby) for a second visit — this time focus on the tech side. Visit the Akihabara UDX building's free tech exhibitions or browse the latest gadgets at Yodobashi Camera. Have dinner in the area.

meals.breakfast: Coffee and melon pan from a local Yanaka bakery for around ¥300–¥400
meals.lunch: Menchi katsu (deep-fried minced meat cutlet) from a Yanaka Ginza stall for around ¥200–¥300, plus other street snacks totaling ¥600–¥800
meals.dinner: Tsukemen (dipping ramen) in Akihabara for around ¥900–¥1,100

day_by_day.notes: Yanaka is a wonderful antidote to Tokyo's modernity — very few tourists and highly authentic. The area around Nezu Shrine is also home to several small, photogenic alleyways. Bring your camera.

day_by_day.morning: Take the train to Ikebukuro — explore Sunshine City complex (free to enter, browse the aquarium exterior and indoor theme park area). Visit the free observation areas of Sunshine 60 building exterior plaza. Explore Otome Road for anime and manga culture.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the free Rikkyo University campus (beautiful Gothic architecture) nearby. Then head to Sugamo — nicknamed 'Harajuku for grandmas' — a charming traditional shopping street popular with elderly locals. Try red-colored dagashi (traditional candies) and browse folk remedy shops.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the Tsukiji area. Visit the Tsukiji Honganji Temple (free) illuminated at night — a stunning Indo-Saracenic style Buddhist temple. Walk along the Sumida River embankment for evening city views.

meals.breakfast: Convenience store morning set for around ¥300–¥400
meals.lunch: Budget set lunch (teishoku) at a local restaurant in Ikebukuro for around ¥800–¥1,000
meals.dinner: Nabe (hot pot) at a budget restaurant near Tsukiji for around ¥1,200–¥1,500

day_by_day.notes: Sugamo is a wonderfully authentic slice of traditional Tokyo life — very different from the tourist areas. The Jizo-dori shopping street has been operating for centuries.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the National Museum of Nature and Science in Ueno (¥630 entry) — excellent exhibits on Japanese science, technology history, and natural history. Spend 2–3 hours exploring the comprehensive collections.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the rest of Ueno Park — visit the Tokyo National Museum exterior and free garden (full museum entry ¥1,000 if interested in Japanese art and culture). Browse the Ameyoko Market for cheap goods and street food. Visit Ueno Zoo if budget allows (¥600).
day_by_day.evening: Head to Koenji — a bohemian neighborhood known for vintage shops, live music venues, and indie culture. Browse the free vintage clothing stores and record shops. Enjoy the local bar scene.

meals.breakfast: Tamagoyaki sandwich from Tsukiji market stall for around ¥400–¥500
meals.lunch: Udon at a budget udon chain (Marugame Seimen) near Ueno for around ¥500–¥700
meals.dinner: Izakaya dinner in Koenji — order small plates (tsumami) to keep costs down, around ¥1,500–¥2,000 including drinks

day_by_day.notes: Friday evening in Koenji is lively with locals. The area has a strong vintage and subculture scene — very different from mainstream Shibuya or Harajuku. Check if any free live music events are happening.

day_by_day.morning: Take a day trip to Nikko (about 2 hours by budget Tobu Railway — around ¥1,400 one way). Visit the UNESCO World Heritage Tosho-gu Shrine complex — ornate and historically significant. Explore the shrine grounds and surrounding cedar forest.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Nikko — visit Rinno-ji Temple and the Yomeimon Gate (the most ornate gate in Japan). Walk the Kanmangafuchi Abyss — a free riverside path lined with mossy stone Jizo statues through a forest gorge.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Tokyo by early evening. Rest and have a relaxed dinner near the hotel in Tsukiji.

meals.breakfast: Onigiri from convenience store before departure for around ¥300
meals.lunch: Yuba (tofu skin) cuisine bento — Nikko's local specialty — from a market stall for around ¥800–¥1,200
meals.dinner: Ramen or soba near Tsukiji for around ¥700–¥900

day_by_day.notes: Use the Tobu Railway Nikko Pass for a discounted day trip (around ¥2,670 round trip from Asakusa including unlimited Nikko bus rides). Nikko entry fees total around ¥1,300 for the main sites. Budget ¥5,000–¥6,000 total for this day trip.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the teamLab Planets in Toyosu (book in advance, ¥3,200) — a different and equally spectacular digital art experience focused on immersive water and light installations. This is a must for tech-culture enthusiasts.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Toyosu Market (the new wholesale fish market that replaced Tsukiji) — visit the free outer market and observation decks overlooking the tuna auction area. Browse the fresh seafood restaurants in the market building.
day_by_day.evening: Final evening in Shibuya — visit the Shibuya Sky observation deck (¥2,000) for a spectacular 360-degree rooftop view of Tokyo at night — a fitting finale. Walk through Shibuya one last time and enjoy the energy.

meals.breakfast: Tsukiji Outer Market — final breakfast of fresh sushi and miso soup for around ¥1,000–¥1,500
meals.lunch: Fresh seafood don (rice bowl) at Toyosu Market restaurant for around ¥1,200–¥1,800
meals.dinner: Splurge slightly on a farewell yakiniku (grilled meat) dinner in Shibuya — budget set for around ¥2,000–¥2,500

day_by_day.notes: Book teamLab Planets well in advance — it sells out on weekends. Shibuya Sky tickets should also be booked online to save time and sometimes money. This is your second-to-last day so consider buying any remaining souvenirs.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning — revisit your favorite spot near Tsukiji for a last breakfast. Pack and check out of the hotel. Store luggage at the hotel or at a coin locker at the nearest subway station (¥300–¥500).
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend your last afternoon in Nihonbashi — Tokyo's historic commercial heart, just a short walk from Tsukiji. Visit the free Nihonbashi Bridge (the zero-kilometer marker of all Japanese roads), explore the Coredo shopping complex, and browse the Mitsukoshi department store basement food hall (depachika) for incredible food displays.
day_by_day.evening: Collect luggage and head to the airport. Take the Narita Express or Airport Limousine Bus. Allow at least 2.5–3 hours before your flight for travel and check-in.

meals.breakfast: Final Tsukiji Outer Market breakfast — splurge on a fresh sashimi set for around ¥1,500
meals.lunch: Depachika (department store basement) food hall at Mitsukoshi — pick up premium bento or wagashi sweets for around ¥800–¥1,200
meals.dinner: Airport food or convenience store meal before the flight for around ¥500–¥800

day_by_day.notes: Use remaining Suica card balance at the airport convenience stores or restaurants — you can refund the ¥500 deposit at airport Suica machines. Buy any last-minute omiyage (souvenirs) at the airport duty-free or at a Don Quijote store before heading out. Safe travels!

trip_options.title: Classic Tokyo, Japan Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at airport at 13:00 — clear customs, collect luggage, and take the Narita Express or Limousine Bus to Tsukiji. Check in to your boutique stay and freshen up.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a relaxed first walk through the Tsukiji Outer Market — browse the food stalls, specialty kitchen shops, and seafood vendors to soak in the neighborhood atmosphere. Pick up a tamagoyaki (Japanese rolled omelette) or fresh oysters from a street vendor as a snack.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Hamarikyu Gardens (a 10-minute walk from Tsukiji) for a peaceful evening stroll along the tidal pond. Then settle in for dinner at a local izakaya near Tsukiji to decompress from the flight.

meals.breakfast: Meal on the plane or grab an onigiri and green tea from a convenience store (7-Eleven or FamilyMart) near the hotel upon arrival.
meals.lunch: Skip or grab a light snack at Tsukiji Outer Market — try a fresh tuna skewer or tamagoyaki from a market stall (¥300–¥800).
meals.dinner: Izakaya dinner near Tsukiji — try Tsukiji Sushiko or a neighborhood yakitori spot. Budget ¥2,000–¥3,500 per person for grilled skewers, small plates, and a beer.

day_by_day.notes: Jet lag may hit hard — keep Day 1 light and low-key. Pick up a Suica or Pasmo IC card at the airport for seamless transit throughout the trip. Tsukiji Outer Market closes around 14:00–15:00 so even a late afternoon visit catches the tail end of activity.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up early (jet lag may help!) and visit Tsukiji Outer Market at its liveliest between 7:00–10:00. Enjoy a sushi breakfast at one of the iconic market sushi counters — this is one of Tokyo's great culinary rituals.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take the subway to Akihabara (Electric Town) — Tokyo's legendary tech and electronics district. Explore multi-floor electronics stores like Yodobashi Camera and Akihabara Radio Kaikan, browse retro game shops, and dive into the unique maid café culture. Visit a retro gaming floor to see Japan's deep tech nostalgia.
day_by_day.evening: Stay in Akihabara for dinner and explore the neon-lit streets after dark — the district transforms beautifully at night. Visit a themed café or grab ramen at a local shop.

meals.breakfast: Sushi breakfast at Tsukiji Outer Market — try Sushi Dai or Daiwa Sushi for a counter experience. Budget ¥1,500–¥2,500 for a full set.
meals.lunch: Akihabara lunch — try a curry rice (kare raisu) set at a local restaurant or a donburi bowl. Budget ¥800–¥1,500.
meals.dinner: Ramen at a popular Akihabara shop such as Fuunji-style tsukemen or a tonkotsu spot. Budget ¥900–¥1,400.

day_by_day.notes: Akihabara is best explored on foot — the main street (Chuo-dori) and the side alleys both have treasures. Many electronics shops have tax-free counters for tourists — bring your passport. Maid cafés are a unique cultural experience; entry fees typically ¥500–¥1,000 plus food/drink order.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Senso-ji Temple in Asakusa — Tokyo's oldest and most iconic temple. Arrive by 8:00–9:00 to beat the crowds. Walk Nakamise-dori shopping street for traditional crafts, snacks, and souvenirs. Climb the nearby Asakusa Culture Tourist Information Center for a free panoramic view.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Yanaka neighborhood — one of Tokyo's best-preserved old shitamachi (downtown) areas. Stroll through Yanaka Ginza shopping street, browse independent craft shops, and wander the atmospheric Yanaka Cemetery (cherry blossoms may still be lingering in mid-April).
day_by_day.evening: Return to the Ginza area (close to your hotel) for an evening walk along the upscale shopping boulevard. Window-shop the flagship stores and enjoy the illuminated streetscape. Dinner in Ginza or Shimbashi.

meals.breakfast: Traditional Japanese breakfast set at a kissaten (old-school coffee shop) near Asakusa — toast, egg, and coffee for ¥500–¥800.
meals.lunch: Yanaka lunch — try a local soba restaurant or a casual tempura set. Budget ¥1,000–¥1,800.
meals.dinner: Shimbashi salaryman district — excellent value yakitori or kushikatsu restaurants popular with Tokyo office workers. Budget ¥2,000–¥3,000.

day_by_day.notes: Mid-April in Tokyo often still has late cherry blossoms (sakura) — Yanaka Cemetery and the Sumida River near Asakusa are beautiful spots. Wear comfortable walking shoes for Yanaka's hilly streets. Senso-ji is free to enter.

day_by_day.morning: Head to teamLab Planets in Toyosu (20 minutes from Tsukiji) — an immersive digital art museum that merges technology and art in a breathtaking way. Book tickets online in advance. This is a perfect intersection of tech culture and culture.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Toyosu Market (the modern replacement to the original Tsukiji wholesale market) — take the observation deck tour to watch the famous tuna auctions in action (viewing areas available). Then walk or cycle along the Toyosu waterfront.
day_by_day.evening: Take the Yurikamome monorail from Toyosu to Odaiba — Tokyo's futuristic artificial island. Visit DiverCity Tokyo Plaza, see the life-sized Gundam statue, and enjoy the stunning nighttime skyline view of Rainbow Bridge and the city.

meals.breakfast: Grab a morning pastry and coffee from a local bakery near the hotel or a convenience store.
meals.lunch: Toyosu sushi lunch — several sushi restaurants near the market serve ultra-fresh sets. Budget ¥2,000–¥3,500.
meals.dinner: Odaiba — dine at a restaurant with a bay view inside DiverCity or Aqua City Odaiba mall. Try Japanese BBQ (yakiniku) or a seafood restaurant. Budget ¥2,500–¥4,000.

day_by_day.notes: teamLab Planets tickets must be booked online in advance — they sell out weeks ahead, especially on weekends. Arrive at the venue 15 minutes early. Odaiba is great for evening photos of the Tokyo skyline reflected in the bay.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Harajuku — start with Meiji Jingu Shrine, a serene forested Shinto shrine dedicated to Emperor Meiji. Then walk through Yoyogi Park (one of Tokyo's largest parks, lovely in spring) and observe local life on a Sunday morning.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Takeshita Street in Harajuku for Tokyo's wild youth fashion culture, then transition to the adjacent Omotesando boulevard for its sophisticated architecture and flagship concept stores. Visit the Omotesando Hills complex (designed by Tadao Ando) for design inspiration.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Shibuya for the famous Shibuya Crossing — best experienced at dusk or night when the neon lights are blazing. Visit Shibuya Sky observation deck for a panoramic 360° city view at sunset.

meals.breakfast: Harajuku crepe from a street stall on Takeshita Street — a Tokyo institution. Budget ¥500–¥800.
meals.lunch: Omotesando lunch — try a Japanese-style pasta or a café set lunch in one of the stylish side-street cafés. Budget ¥1,200–¥2,000.
meals.dinner: Shibuya dinner — explore the food floors (depachika) in Shibuya Hikarie or grab a hearty gyudon (beef bowl) at Yoshinoya or a more upscale shabu-shabu set. Budget ¥1,500–¥3,000.

day_by_day.notes: Shibuya Sky observation deck tickets are best booked online (¥2,000 per person). The crossing is most dramatic at rush hour around 17:00–19:00. Sunday mornings at Yoyogi Park sometimes feature live music, cosplay gatherings, and dance groups — a uniquely Tokyo experience.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Edo-Tokyo Museum in Ryogoku — an outstanding museum covering 400 years of Tokyo's history from the Edo period to the modern era. Perfect for understanding the city's cultural depth. The museum has full-scale reconstructions of Edo-era streets.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to the nearby Ryogoku Kokugikan (sumo arena) — even if there's no tournament, the sumo museum inside is free. If timing aligns with a tournament (check the schedule), tickets can be purchased in advance. Explore the Ryogoku neighborhood, known for chanko-nabe (sumo wrestler stew).
day_by_day.evening: Return toward Ginza and explore the Ginza Six complex — Tokyo's premier luxury department store with excellent basement food halls (depachika). Pick up premium snacks or sweets for the trip.

meals.breakfast: Japanese breakfast at a neighborhood teishoku restaurant near the hotel — grilled fish, rice, miso soup, and pickles. Budget ¥700–¥1,200.
meals.lunch: Ryogoku chanko-nabe lunch — the neighborhood is famous for this hearty sumo stew. Try Chanko Tomoegata or a similar local spot. Budget ¥1,500–¥2,500.
meals.dinner: Ginza depachika dinner — assemble a gourmet meal from the basement food halls of Ginza Six or Matsuya Ginza: premium sushi, wagyu bento, seasonal side dishes, and Japanese sweets. Budget ¥2,000–¥3,500.

day_by_day.notes: Check the sumo tournament schedule before your trip — the Tokyo tournaments (honbasho) are held in January, May, and September at Ryogoku. The Edo-Tokyo Museum admission is approximately ¥600. The depachika dinner is a quintessential Tokyo food experience.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Nikko — take the Tobu Nikko Line from Asakusa (approximately 2 hours). Explore the UNESCO World Heritage Tosho-gu Shrine, one of Japan's most ornate and historically significant shrines, nestled in a cedar forest in the mountains.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Nikko — visit Rinno-ji Temple, the Yomeimon Gate (nicknamed the 'Gate of a Day' for how long you could spend admiring it), and Shinkyo Bridge. The surrounding nature is lush and spectacular in mid-April.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Tokyo by early evening. Enjoy a quiet dinner near the hotel to rest after a full day of travel.

meals.breakfast: Grab an ekiben (train bento box) from Asakusa station or a convenience store breakfast before boarding.
meals.lunch: Nikko yuba (tofu skin) cuisine — a local specialty. Try a yuba set lunch at a restaurant near the shrine complex. Budget ¥1,500–¥2,500.
meals.dinner: Return to Tsukiji area — enjoy a simple but satisfying dinner at a neighborhood soba restaurant. Budget ¥1,000–¥1,800.

day_by_day.notes: Buy a Tobu Nikko Pass for unlimited train and bus rides in the Nikko area (approximately ¥4,780 from Asakusa). The Tosho-gu entry fee is ¥1,300. Start early to maximize time — first train from Asakusa around 7:30. Wear layers as Nikko is cooler than Tokyo.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Tokyo National Museum in Ueno — Japan's largest museum with an extraordinary collection of samurai swords, ancient pottery, Buddhist sculptures, ukiyo-e prints, and more. Spend 2–3 hours exploring the main Honkan building.
day_by_day.afternoon: Stroll through Ueno Park and Ueno Zoo (optional), then head to Ameyoko Market — a lively open-air market street beneath the train tracks selling food, clothing, cosmetics, and goods at bargain prices. A great contrast to Ginza's luxury.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Koenji or Shimokitazawa (indie Tokyo neighborhoods) for an alternative evening — vinyl record shops, vintage clothing stores, live music venues, and casual bars. Shimokitazawa is especially beloved for its bohemian atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Ueno area kissaten breakfast — a classic morning coffee and toast set. Budget ¥600–¥900.
meals.lunch: Ameyoko Market street food lunch — grilled seafood, gyoza, fried chicken, and fresh fruit. Budget ¥800–¥1,500.
meals.dinner: Shimokitazawa — try a cozy curry restaurant (the neighborhood is known for its curry spots) or a small izakaya. Budget ¥1,500–¥2,500.

day_by_day.notes: Tokyo National Museum admission is ¥1,000. Check for special exhibitions which may have separate fees. Ameyoko is busiest in the afternoon and has a great energy — bargaining is occasionally possible with vendors. Shimokitazawa is about 25 minutes from Ueno by subway.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Mori Art Museum in Roppongi Hills — one of Tokyo's top contemporary art institutions with stunning city views from the adjacent Tokyo City View observation deck. The museum focuses on cutting-edge international and Japanese contemporary art.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Roppongi's art triangle — visit the National Art Center Tokyo (free entry to the building, Japan's largest exhibition space with a dramatic Kisho Kurokawa-designed exterior) and 21_21 Design Sight in Midtown Tokyo (a design museum co-founded by Issey Miyake).
day_by_day.evening: Roppongi comes alive at night — enjoy the cosmopolitan nightlife atmosphere. Have dinner at one of the many international or Japanese restaurants in Roppongi Hills or Tokyo Midtown.

meals.breakfast: Hotel area breakfast or a café near Tsukiji. Try a Japanese-style morning set at a local spot.
meals.lunch: Roppongi Hills restaurant floor — wide variety of options from sushi to Italian. Try a Japanese set lunch (teishoku). Budget ¥1,500–¥2,500.
meals.dinner: Tokyo Midtown dinner — explore the restaurant floors for quality Japanese cuisine. Try a kaiseki-lite set meal or a tempura restaurant. Budget ¥3,000–¥5,000 for a mid-range splurge.

day_by_day.notes: Mori Art Museum + Tokyo City View combined ticket is approximately ¥2,000. The observation deck at night is spectacular — consider returning after dinner for the view. 21_21 Design Sight admission is ¥1,400. This is a great day for design and art lovers.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Shinjuku Gyoen National Garden — one of Tokyo's most beautiful parks, especially in mid-April when late cherry blossoms and early spring flowers overlap. A peaceful oasis within the bustling city.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Shinjuku's contrasts — visit Kabukicho (Tokyo's entertainment district) in the afternoon to see the famous Robot Restaurant area and the new Godzilla head atop Toho Cinema. Then visit the Tokyo Metropolitan Government Building for a free observation deck with panoramic views.
day_by_day.evening: Spend the evening in Shinjuku — explore the Golden Gai (a maze of tiny atmospheric bars, each seating only 5–8 people) and Omoide Yokocho (Memory Lane) for yakitori and a truly old Tokyo atmosphere under the train tracks.

meals.breakfast: Shinjuku morning — grab a coffee and pastry at a local bakery or Doutor Coffee (affordable Japanese chain). Budget ¥400–¥700.
meals.lunch: Shinjuku lunch — try a katsu curry (breaded pork cutlet with curry) at Saboten or a similar tonkatsu restaurant. Budget ¥1,000–¥1,800.
meals.dinner: Omoide Yokocho (Memory Lane) — sit at a tiny yakitori counter, order skewers of grilled chicken, and drink cold beer or sake. Budget ¥2,000–¥3,000 for a full experience.

day_by_day.notes: Shinjuku Gyoen entry is ¥500. The Tokyo Metropolitan Government Building observation deck is free but closes at 22:30 (north tower). Golden Gai bars often have a small cover charge (¥500–¥1,000) — check before sitting down. This is one of Tokyo's most memorable evening experiences.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Kamakura — take the JR Yokosuka Line from Tokyo Station (about 1 hour). Visit the iconic Kotoku-in Temple with the Great Buddha (Daibutsu) — a 13-meter bronze statue dating from 1252. Then explore Hase-dera Temple with its hillside garden and coastal views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk the Daibutsu Hiking Trail through bamboo groves and forested hills connecting several Zen temples. Alternatively, stroll through Komachi-dori shopping street for local crafts, shirasu (whitebait) dishes, and matcha sweets.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Tokyo by early evening. Enjoy a relaxed dinner near the hotel — perhaps a final visit to the Tsukiji Outer Market area for a seafood dinner.

meals.breakfast: Grab an ekiben from Tokyo Station before boarding — try a classic Makunouchi bento with seasonal items. Budget ¥900–¥1,500.
meals.lunch: Kamakura shirasu don (rice bowl with fresh whitebait) at a restaurant near Hase Station — a local specialty. Budget ¥1,200–¥2,000.
meals.dinner: Tsukiji area seafood dinner — try a chirashi don (scattered sushi rice bowl) or a fresh sashimi set at a local restaurant. Budget ¥2,000–¥3,500.

day_by_day.notes: Kamakura is best explored with a day pass — the Enoshima-Kamakura Free Pass covers trains and the Enoden tram (¥1,640 from Shinjuku). The Great Buddha admission is ¥300. You can enter the hollow interior for an additional ¥20. Mid-April weather in Kamakura is typically mild and pleasant.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Shiodome and the Panasonic Shiodome Museum of Art (rotating exhibitions) — a lesser-known gem close to your hotel. Then walk to Hama-rikyu Gardens again for a more leisurely visit — rent a boat or enjoy the traditional teahouse for matcha and wagashi (Japanese sweets).
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Kiyosumi-Shirakawa neighborhood — Tokyo's specialty coffee capital. This trendy district has a high concentration of third-wave coffee roasters (Blue Bottle Coffee Japan opened its first location here) alongside art galleries and the Tokyo Museum of Contemporary Art.
day_by_day.evening: Final evening in Tokyo — return to Ginza for a farewell dinner. Treat yourself to a slightly elevated dining experience — a proper sushi counter, a teppanyaki restaurant, or a traditional kappo (counter-style Japanese cuisine) meal.

meals.breakfast: Hama-rikyu teahouse — enjoy a bowl of matcha and a wagashi sweet in the traditional garden setting. Budget ¥500–¥800 (includes garden entry ¥300).
meals.lunch: Kiyosumi-Shirakawa café lunch — pair specialty coffee with a light lunch at one of the neighborhood's café-restaurants. Budget ¥1,200–¥2,000.
meals.dinner: Ginza farewell dinner — splurge slightly at a quality sushi counter (omakase lunch-style pricing at dinner) or a tempura restaurant. Budget ¥4,000–¥7,000 for a memorable final meal.

day_by_day.notes: Kiyosumi-Shirakawa is about 15 minutes by subway from Tsukiji. The Tokyo Museum of Contemporary Art (MOT) admission varies by exhibition (approximately ¥500–¥1,500). For the farewell dinner, consider booking in advance — Ginza Sushi Yoshitake or Tempura Kondo are well-regarded mid-to-upper range options.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Tokyo — take a slow walk through the Tsukiji Outer Market one last time for breakfast. Pick up last-minute food souvenirs: high-quality Japanese knives, dried bonito flakes, wasabi, or premium teas from the market shops.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on departure time — visit the Intermediateque (Intermediatheque) museum inside KITTE building near Tokyo Station for free (a fascinating collection merging the University of Tokyo's natural history specimens with design and art). Then browse KITTE's curated Japanese craft and food shops for final souvenirs.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the airport for departure. Take the Narita Express from Tokyo Station or a Limousine Bus from Ginza/Tsukiji area. Allow at least 2.5–3 hours before departure for check-in and security.

meals.breakfast: Final Tsukiji Outer Market breakfast — fresh sushi, tamagoyaki, and a hot bowl of miso soup from the market vendors. Budget ¥1,000–¥2,000.
meals.lunch: KITTE building restaurant floor or a quick but quality ramen at Tokyo Station's Ramen Street (inside the station). Budget ¥1,000–¥1,800.
meals.dinner: Airport dinner at Narita or Haneda — both airports have excellent Japanese restaurant options including soba, sushi, and tonkatsu. Budget ¥1,500–¥2,500.

day_by_day.notes: Intermediateque (KITTE, 2F–3F) is free and open Tuesday–Sunday. KITTE's basement and floors have excellent Japanese regional food products and crafts for last-minute gift shopping. Confirm your flight terminal early — Narita has three terminals. Leave the hotel by early afternoon if your flight is in the evening.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Tokyo, Japan Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

experiences.name: Tsukiji Outer Market Food Tour
experiences.description: Explore the bustling Tsukiji Outer Market, sampling fresh sushi, tamagoyaki, and street snacks from legendary vendors. Interact with local fishmongers and food artisans who have operated for generations, giving you an authentic taste of Tokyo's deep culinary heritage.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival & Check-In: Flight LH lands at Narita/Haneda at 13:00. Clear customs and immigration, then take the Narita Express or a private luxury transfer to your boutique stay in Tsukiji, Chuo City. Check in, freshen up, and settle into your room.
day_by_day.afternoon: Tsukiji Outer Market Orientation Stroll: After settling in, take a leisurely walk through the iconic Tsukiji Outer Market — just steps from your hotel. Sample fresh tamagoyaki (Japanese rolled omelette), uni (sea urchin), and premium tuna sashimi from the legendary stalls. Pick up a matcha soft-serve from a local vendor and soak in the vibrant atmosphere.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at Sushi Saito (or comparable Michelin-starred sushi-ya in Ginza): Head to nearby Ginza (10 min by taxi) for an omakase sushi experience at one of Tokyo's finest counters. Expect 15–20 courses of meticulously selected seasonal fish, aged vinegared rice, and house-made tamago. Pair with premium sake selected by the itamae.

meals.breakfast: On the flight or at the airport — grab a light bento or airport ramen at Narita's Ichiran ramen counter before your transfer.
meals.lunch: Tsukiji Outer Market street snacks: fresh oysters, grilled scallops, and tuna sashimi bites from market vendors (¥3,000–¥5,000 per person).
meals.dinner: Omakase dinner at a Michelin-starred Ginza sushi counter such as Sushi Yoshitake or Sushi Saito (reservation essential, ¥30,000–¥50,000 per person).

day_by_day.notes: Jet lag tip: Stay awake until at least 21:00 local time to reset your body clock. Keep Day 1 light and enjoyable. Pre-book your Ginza omakase well in advance — these seats fill months ahead. A private car transfer from the airport (~¥20,000–¥30,000) is recommended for comfort after a long flight.

day_by_day.morning: Tsukiji Outer Market Food Tour (Guided Premium Experience): Join an exclusive small-group or private guided food tour of Tsukiji Outer Market starting at 08:00. A knowledgeable local guide leads you through the labyrinthine lanes, introducing you to veteran vendors. Taste premium tuna cuts, house-made dashi, pickled vegetables, fresh mochi, and rare seasonal seafood. Learn the history of the market and the art of Japanese knife-making at a specialist shop.
day_by_day.afternoon: Hamarikyu Gardens & Tokyo Bay Cruise: A 5-minute walk from Tsukiji brings you to the stunning Hamarikyu Gardens, a 17th-century feudal lord's garden with tidal ponds, pine trees, and a traditional teahouse. Enjoy a matcha ceremony at the Nakajima-no-Ochaya teahouse on the island. Afterward, board a Sumida River water bus for a scenic 40-minute cruise to Asakusa, passing under historic bridges.
day_by_day.evening: Asakusa Cultural Evening: Explore Senso-ji Temple at dusk when the crowds thin and the lanterns glow beautifully. Browse Nakamise-dori for artisan souvenirs. Dinner at Komagata Dojo, a 200-year-old loach restaurant beloved by Tokyoites, or opt for a kaiseki dinner at Asakusa Imahan for premium Wagyu sukiyaki.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the market during the food tour — fresh tamago sando, grilled fish, miso soup, and Japanese pickles from Tsukiji vendors.
meals.lunch: Teahouse snacks (wagashi sweets and matcha) at Hamarikyu's Nakajima-no-Ochaya, followed by a light soba lunch at a nearby Nihonbashi soba restaurant (¥2,000–¥4,000).
meals.dinner: Wagyu sukiyaki omakase at Asakusa Imahan or traditional loach hotpot at Komagata Dojo (¥15,000–¥25,000 per person).

day_by_day.notes: Hamarikyu Gardens opens at 09:00 (¥300 entry). The Sumida River water bus runs regularly and tickets can be purchased at the pier. Senso-ji is most atmospheric at golden hour — plan to arrive around 17:30.

day_by_day.morning: Akihabara Tech & Electronics District: Take the JR Yamanote Line to Akihabara, Tokyo's legendary 'Electric Town.' Explore multi-story electronics megastores like Yodobashi Akiba, browse the latest robotics, gaming peripherals, AI gadgets, and rare tech collectibles. Visit the Akihabara Radio Center for vintage electronics and retro computing nostalgia. Stop at a specialist drone or VR shop for hands-on demos of cutting-edge consumer technology.
day_by_day.afternoon: teamLab Planets or teamLab Borderless (Digital Art Museum): Head to the immersive digital art universe created by teamLab, where technology and art merge in breathtaking installations. Walk through infinite crystal universes, wade through a garden of flowers, and lose yourself in mirror rooms filled with light and sound. Book premium timed-entry tickets well in advance. Afterward, explore the nearby Toyosu area.
day_by_day.evening: Ginza Luxury Shopping & Dinner: Return to Ginza for an evening of world-class shopping at Ginza Six, Mitsukoshi, and international flagship boutiques. Dine at a celebrated French-Japanese fusion restaurant such as L'Osier (three Michelin stars) or enjoy a premium tempura omakase at Tempura Kondo.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a visit to a traditional Japanese breakfast café near Tsukiji — grilled fish set, rice, miso soup, and pickles (¥1,500–¥3,000).
meals.lunch: Akihabara lunch at a high-end Japanese curry house or ramen specialist — try Curry Up or a premium tonkotsu counter (¥1,500–¥3,000).
meals.dinner: Three-Michelin-star French-Japanese dinner at L'Osier in Ginza or premium tempura omakase at Tempura Kondo (¥25,000–¥60,000 per person).

day_by_day.notes: teamLab venues require advance online booking — slots sell out weeks ahead. Akihabara is best explored on weekday mornings before crowds build. Ginza shops typically close at 20:00–21:00, so plan dinner reservations for 19:30 or later.

day_by_day.morning: Shibuya Crossing & Omotesando Architecture Walk: Start at the world-famous Shibuya Scramble Crossing — observe the choreographed pedestrian ballet from the Mag's Park observation deck or Starbucks Reserve Roastery. Then walk north to Omotesando, Tokyo's 'Champs-Élysées,' admiring the architectural masterpieces: Tadao Ando's Omotesando Hills, Toyo Ito's Tod's building, and SANAA's Dior boutique. Browse concept stores and luxury flagship shops.
day_by_day.afternoon: Nezu Museum & Yanaka Old Town: Take a taxi to the serene Nezu Museum in Minami-Aoyama, housing an extraordinary collection of pre-modern Asian art including ancient bronzes, ceramics, and calligraphy, set within a beautiful garden. Then head to Yanaka, one of Tokyo's best-preserved historic neighborhoods, for a slow afternoon walk through old shitamachi streets, traditional craft shops, and independent galleries.
day_by_day.evening: Roppongi Arts & Fine Dining: Head to Roppongi for a visit to Mori Art Museum (open until 22:00) for contemporary art with panoramic Tokyo skyline views from the 52nd floor. Dine at Azabu Juban's Quintessence (three Michelin stars) or enjoy a premium teppanyaki experience at Ukai-tei Roppongi.

meals.breakfast: Brunch at Omotesando's Café Kitsuné or a premium eggs Benedict at bills Japan (¥2,500–¥4,000).
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the Nezu Museum Garden Café — seasonal Japanese bento set amid the tranquil garden (¥3,000–¥5,000).
meals.dinner: Three-Michelin-star dinner at Quintessence in Azabu Juban or premium teppanyaki at Ukai-tei Roppongi (¥30,000–¥60,000 per person).

day_by_day.notes: Nezu Museum is closed on Mondays. Mori Art Museum's city views are spectacular after dark — try to arrive around 20:00 for the best experience. Yanaka is best explored on foot; wear comfortable shoes.

day_by_day.morning: Shinjuku Gyoen National Garden (Cherry Blossom Season): In mid-April, Shinjuku Gyoen may still have late-blooming sakura or fresh spring foliage. Spend a peaceful morning in this magnificent 58-hectare garden, featuring French formal, English landscape, and Japanese traditional garden sections. Visit the large greenhouse with tropical plants. Enjoy the tranquility before the crowds arrive.
day_by_day.afternoon: Shinjuku Tech & Pop Culture Exploration: Explore the west side of Shinjuku for Tokyo's skyscraper district, then cross to Kabukicho and the Golden Gai area. Visit Yodobashi Camera Multimedia Shinjuku for the latest tech. Head to Takashimaya Times Square for its impressive food halls and luxury retail. Explore the fascinating Robot Restaurant area and the neon-lit alleys of Omoide Yokocho (Memory Lane).
day_by_day.evening: Omakase Dinner & Shinjuku Jazz Bar: Dine at a premium kaiseki restaurant in Shinjuku such as Nakamura or a high-end yakitori counter in the area. Afterward, unwind at a sophisticated jazz bar like DUG or Pit Inn in Shinjuku, a beloved institution of Tokyo's jazz scene, sipping premium Japanese whisky.

meals.breakfast: Traditional Japanese breakfast set at a teahouse near Shinjuku Gyoen — rice, grilled salmon, pickles, and tofu (¥2,000–¥3,500).
meals.lunch: Premium ramen at Fuunji (tsukemen specialist) or a Wagyu beef bowl at a high-end gyudon restaurant in Shinjuku (¥3,000–¥6,000).
meals.dinner: Kaiseki dinner at a Shinjuku ryotei or premium yakitori omakase at Toriki (¥20,000–¥35,000 per person), followed by Japanese whisky at a Shinjuku jazz bar.

day_by_day.notes: Shinjuku Gyoen entry is ¥500; opens at 09:00. No alcohol permitted inside the garden. The Golden Gai area is a fascinating cluster of tiny bars — best explored in the evening. Book jazz bar seats in advance on weekends.

day_by_day.morning: Harajuku & Meiji Jingu Shrine: Begin with a serene morning visit to Meiji Jingu Shrine, Tokyo's grandest Shinto shrine set within a forested 70-hectare park. Participate in a traditional morning prayer ritual and observe the shrine's architectural grandeur. Then walk to Harajuku's Takeshita Street for a fascinating glimpse into Tokyo's youth fashion culture and creative subcultures.
day_by_day.afternoon: Daikanyama & Nakameguro Lifestyle Districts: Take a short taxi ride to Daikanyama, Tokyo's most stylish neighborhood. Visit the iconic Tsutaya Books (T-Site) — a beautifully designed lifestyle bookstore and cultural hub beloved by creative professionals. Stroll along the Meguro River in Nakameguro, lined with independent boutiques, specialty coffee roasters, and design studios. Browse curated concept stores and artisan shops.
day_by_day.evening: Ebisu Craft Beer & Premium Wagyu Dinner: Visit the Yebisu Beer Museum in Ebisu for a premium tasting of Japan's finest craft beers and a historical tour of the legendary Sapporo Brewery site. Then dine at a top-tier Wagyu steakhouse such as Aragawa (Tokyo's most legendary steakhouse, known for Kobe beef) or Wolfgan Puck's cut in Tokyo for a premium experience.

meals.breakfast: Café breakfast near Meiji Jingu — avocado toast and specialty pour-over coffee at a Harajuku café (¥2,000–¥3,500).
meals.lunch: Artisan lunch at Daikanyama — seasonal Japanese pasta or a gourmet sandwich from a Daikanyama bistro (¥3,000–¥5,000).
meals.dinner: Premium Wagyu steak dinner at Aragawa or a top Ebisu steakhouse (¥40,000–¥80,000 per person for Kobe beef).

day_by_day.notes: Meiji Jingu is free to enter and opens at sunrise. The Tsutaya Books in Daikanyama has an excellent English-language section and a Starbucks Reserve inside. Aragawa is one of the world's most expensive steakhouses — reservations are essential months in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Day Trip to Nikko (UNESCO World Heritage): Take the Tobu Nikko Limited Express from Asakusa (approx. 2 hours) to Nikko, one of Japan's most ornate and historically significant shrine complexes. Explore Tosho-gu Shrine, the lavishly decorated mausoleum of Tokugawa Ieyasu, adorned with gold leaf, intricate carvings, and vibrant lacquerwork. Walk through the cedar-lined Omotesando avenue and visit Rinnoji Temple.
day_by_day.afternoon: Nikko Nature & Waterfalls: After the shrines, take a bus or taxi to Kegon Falls, one of Japan's most spectacular waterfalls, plunging 97 meters into the valley below. Visit Lake Chuzenji nearby for stunning mountain scenery. In spring, the surrounding mountains may still have snow-capped peaks, creating a dramatic contrast with blooming vegetation.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Tokyo & Nihonbashi Dinner: Return to Tokyo by early evening. Head to Nihonbashi, one of Tokyo's most historic commercial districts, for a premium dinner at Nihonbashi Yukari (three Michelin stars, modern Japanese cuisine) or a traditional kappo dining experience at a Nihonbashi ryotei.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at Tokyo Station's premium food hall or a hotel breakfast before departure (¥2,000–¥4,000).
meals.lunch: Yuba (tofu skin) cuisine lunch at a Nikko specialty restaurant — a local delicacy unique to the Nikko area (¥3,000–¥6,000).
meals.dinner: Three-Michelin-star dinner at Nihonbashi Yukari or kappo omakase at a Nihonbashi ryotei (¥25,000–¥45,000 per person).

day_by_day.notes: Purchase a Tobu Nikko All Area Pass for unlimited buses within Nikko. Start early (depart by 07:30) to maximize time at the shrines before tour groups arrive. Nikko can be crowded on weekends — a Tuesday visit is ideal. Wear comfortable walking shoes.

day_by_day.morning: Odaiba Tech & Innovation District: Take the scenic Yurikamome monorail from Shimbashi over Rainbow Bridge to Odaiba, Tokyo's futuristic waterfront district. Visit the National Museum of Emerging Science and Innovation (Miraikan), Japan's premier science and technology museum, featuring ASIMO the robot, a life-size Earth globe, and cutting-edge AI and space exploration exhibits. Explore the Sony ExploraScience interactive tech center.
day_by_day.afternoon: Odaiba Waterfront & Palette Town: Stroll along the Odaiba waterfront promenade with views of Rainbow Bridge and the Tokyo skyline. Visit the Toyota Mega Web showroom for futuristic concept cars and driving simulators. Explore the massive Palette Town complex and the iconic giant Ferris wheel. Head to DiverCity Tokyo for the life-size Gundam statue — a must-see for tech and pop culture enthusiasts.
day_by_day.evening: Shiodome & Caretta Illumination Dinner: Head to Shiodome's Caretta Shopping Center for a premium dinner with panoramic views of Tokyo Bay. Dine at a rooftop restaurant such as Namasté or enjoy French cuisine at a Shiodome hotel restaurant. The Caretta illumination (seasonal) creates a magical atmosphere in the evenings.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a Tsukiji morning market breakfast — fresh fish, rice, and miso soup (¥2,000–¥4,000).
meals.lunch: Odaiba lunch at a premium seafood restaurant in Decks Tokyo Beach or DiverCity — fresh sushi or grilled seafood with Tokyo Bay views (¥4,000–¥8,000).
meals.dinner: Premium French-Japanese dinner at a Shiodome hotel restaurant or Caretta rooftop dining (¥20,000–¥35,000 per person).

day_by_day.notes: Miraikan is closed on Tuesdays. The Yurikamome monorail offers spectacular views of Tokyo Bay — sit at the front of the driverless train for the best experience. The life-size Gundam statue at DiverCity sometimes features timed light and sound shows — check the schedule.

day_by_day.morning: Ueno Museums & Cultural Morning: Explore Tokyo's cultural heartland in Ueno Park. Begin at the Tokyo National Museum (Japan's largest and oldest museum), housing over 110,000 artifacts including samurai armor, Buddhist sculptures, ukiyo-e woodblock prints, and ancient ceramics. Then visit the National Museum of Nature and Science for world-class natural history and science exhibits. The park itself may have late-blooming cherry blossoms or fresh spring greenery.
day_by_day.afternoon: Yanaka Ginza & Traditional Craft Workshops: Walk from Ueno to Yanaka Ginza, a beautifully preserved old-fashioned shopping street with family-run craft shops, pottery studios, and traditional sweet makers. Participate in a private hands-on Japanese craft workshop — options include traditional pottery (setomono), indigo dyeing (aizome), or Japanese calligraphy (shodo) with a master artisan.
day_by_day.evening: Kagurazaka French-Japanese Quartier Dinner: Take a taxi to Kagurazaka, Tokyo's most Parisian neighborhood, with cobblestone alleys, French bistros, and traditional ryotei. Dine at a celebrated Kagurazaka restaurant such as Kohaku (three Michelin stars, innovative Japanese cuisine) or enjoy a premium French dinner at one of the neighborhood's acclaimed bistros.

meals.breakfast: Ueno café breakfast — fresh-baked pastries and specialty coffee near the museum district (¥2,000–¥3,500).
meals.lunch: Traditional Yanaka lunch — handmade soba noodles at a century-old soba-ya or a set lunch at a local Yanaka café (¥2,000–¥4,000).
meals.dinner: Three-Michelin-star dinner at Kohaku in Kagurazaka or premium French-Japanese fusion dinner (¥30,000–¥50,000 per person).

day_by_day.notes: Tokyo National Museum opens at 09:30. Pre-book the craft workshop at least a week in advance through a luxury concierge service or specialist cultural tour operator. Kagurazaka is most atmospheric in the evening when the lanterns are lit.

day_by_day.morning: Toyosu Market (Tuna Auction Observation): Apply in advance for the exclusive tuna auction observation at Toyosu Market (Tsukiji's successor), where the world's most expensive tuna are auctioned at dawn. Arrive at 05:00 for the 05:30 auction — an extraordinary spectacle of Japanese culinary culture. After the auction, explore the market's premium seafood stalls and enjoy the freshest possible sushi breakfast.
day_by_day.afternoon: Ginza Art Galleries & Cultural Exploration: Return to the hotel to rest, then head to Ginza's world-class art galleries. Visit the Itabashi Art Museum, the Shiseido Gallery, or the Ginza Graphic Gallery for contemporary Japanese art and design exhibitions. Browse Ginza's luxury stationery shops (Itoya, a 7-floor stationery paradise) and high-end Japanese craft stores.
day_by_day.evening: Kabuki-za Theatre Performance: Attend a traditional Kabuki performance at the iconic Kabuki-za Theatre in Ginza — one of Japan's greatest cultural experiences. Single-act tickets (hitomaku-mi) are available for shorter viewing. The elaborate costumes, dramatic makeup, and centuries-old theatrical traditions are mesmerizing. Afterward, dine at a premium restaurant in the Kabuki-za Tower.

meals.breakfast: Ultra-fresh sushi breakfast at Toyosu Market's premium sushi restaurants — the best tuna you'll ever taste, served at 06:00–07:00 (¥5,000–¥15,000 per person).
meals.lunch: Light lunch at a Ginza café or the Itoya rooftop restaurant — seasonal Japanese salad and premium sandwiches (¥3,000–¥5,000).
meals.dinner: Post-Kabuki kaiseki dinner at a Ginza ryotei or premium restaurant in the Kabuki-za Tower complex (¥20,000–¥35,000 per person).

day_by_day.notes: Toyosu tuna auction observation requires advance lottery application through the Tokyo Metropolitan Central Wholesale Market website — apply 2–3 months ahead. Only 120 observers are allowed per session. Kabuki-za single-act tickets are sold on the day at the theatre box office from 10:00 — arrive early.

day_by_day.morning: Hakone Day Trip — Mt. Fuji Views & Onsen: Take the Romancecar limited express from Shinjuku to Hakone (approx. 85 minutes). On a clear day, enjoy breathtaking views of Mt. Fuji. Visit the Hakone Open Air Museum, Japan's premier outdoor sculpture park featuring works by Henry Moore, Picasso, and leading Japanese sculptors set against mountain scenery. Ride the Hakone Ropeway over volcanic Owakudani for dramatic views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Hakone Lake Ashi & Luxury Ryokan Onsen: Cruise across the serene Lake Ashi on a historic sightseeing boat with Mt. Fuji reflected in the water. Visit the Hakone Checkpoint (Edo-era barrier) for historical context. Check into a luxury ryokan (Gora Kadan or Fujiya Hotel) for an afternoon of traditional Japanese bathing in a private open-air rotenburo onsen with mountain views.
day_by_day.evening: Ryokan Kaiseki Dinner & Return to Tokyo: Enjoy a multi-course kaiseki dinner at the ryokan — an exquisite seasonal feast featuring locally sourced mountain vegetables, river fish, and Wagyu beef, served in your tatami room or a private dining space. Return to Tokyo by late evening on the Romancecar.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast in Tokyo before departure (¥2,000–¥4,000) or breakfast on the Romancecar.
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the Hakone Open Air Museum café or a soba restaurant in Hakone town (¥2,000–¥4,000).
meals.dinner: Full kaiseki dinner at Gora Kadan or Fujiya Hotel ryokan — a 10–12 course seasonal feast (included in ryokan day-use package, ¥30,000–¥60,000 per person).

day_by_day.notes: Mt. Fuji visibility is weather-dependent — check forecasts the night before. The Hakone Free Pass covers most transportation within Hakone. Book the ryokan day-use onsen package (higaeri nyuyoku) well in advance — weekends fill up quickly. Return Romancecar trains to Shinjuku run until approximately 22:00.

day_by_day.morning: Shibuya Scramble Square Observation Deck & Nishiki Market Alternative — Koenji & Shimokitazawa Vintage Culture: Start with breakfast and a visit to the Shibuya Sky observation deck atop Scramble Square (230m high) for a 360-degree panoramic view of Tokyo. Then head to Shimokitazawa, Tokyo's bohemian village, known for its independent theaters, vintage clothing boutiques, record stores, and artisan coffee shops. Browse rare vinyl records and vintage Japanese fashion.
day_by_day.afternoon: Setagaya Boroichi Antique Market (if scheduled) or Bunkamura Cultural Centre: Visit Bunkamura in Shibuya — Tokyo's premier multi-arts complex featuring a concert hall, cinema, museum, and gallery. Check the program for classical music performances, art exhibitions, or theatrical productions. Alternatively, explore the Toguri Museum of Art for exceptional ukiyo-e woodblock print collections.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell Luxury Dinner & Rooftop Bar: For a penultimate night celebration, dine at one of Tokyo's most spectacular rooftop restaurants — Andaz Tokyo's rooftop bar (45th floor, Toranomon Hills) or the Park Hyatt Tokyo's New York Grill (featured in 'Lost in Translation'). Enjoy a final evening of Tokyo's glittering skyline with premium Japanese whisky, champagne, and a world-class meal.

meals.breakfast: Premium hotel breakfast or a specialty coffee and pastry at a Shibuya café (¥2,500–¥4,000).
meals.lunch: Shimokitazawa artisan lunch — handmade pasta at an Italian trattoria or a creative Japanese bento at a neighborhood café (¥2,000–¥4,000).
meals.dinner: New York Grill at Park Hyatt Tokyo or Andaz Tokyo rooftop dining — premium steaks, Japanese-influenced cuisine, and panoramic city views (¥25,000–¥45,000 per person).

day_by_day.notes: Shibuya Sky observation deck tickets can be purchased online in advance (recommended on weekends). Shimokitazawa is best explored on foot — the streets are narrow and pedestrian-friendly. The Park Hyatt New York Grill is iconic and requires advance reservations; request a window table for the best views.

day_by_day.morning: Final Morning in Tsukiji & Souvenir Shopping: Enjoy a final leisurely breakfast at Tsukiji Outer Market — one last round of fresh sushi, tamago, and Japanese pickles from your favorite vendors. Then shop for premium Japanese souvenirs: high-grade matcha from a specialist tea house, artisan Japanese knives from a Tsukiji knife shop, premium sake, wagashi sweets, and handmade ceramics from Nihonbashi Mitsukoshi.
day_by_day.afternoon: Nihonbashi & Coredo Muromachi Farewell Exploration: Spend your final afternoon in Nihonbashi, Tokyo's historic commercial heart. Visit the Coredo Muromachi complex for premium Japanese lifestyle goods, specialty food producers, and artisan craft shops. Stop at the Bank of Japan Currency Museum for a fascinating glimpse into Japan's financial history. Enjoy a final matcha ceremony at a traditional Nihonbashi tea house.
day_by_day.evening: Airport Transfer & Departure: Pack, check out of your boutique hotel in Tsukiji, and arrange a private luxury car transfer to Narita or Haneda Airport. Allow 2–3 hours for the airport journey on a Monday evening. Enjoy a final premium meal at the airport's excellent restaurant options (Narita's Sushi Kyubey or Haneda's premium food hall) before your departure flight.

meals.breakfast: Final Tsukiji Outer Market breakfast — fresh sushi, tamagoyaki, grilled scallops, and miso soup from market vendors (¥3,000–¥6,000).
meals.lunch: Premium lunch at Coredo Muromachi — seasonal Japanese cuisine at one of the complex's acclaimed restaurants (¥5,000–¥10,000).
meals.dinner: Airport farewell dinner at Narita's Sushi Kyubey or Haneda ANA FESTA premium food hall — fresh sushi and a final glass of Japanese whisky (¥5,000–¥15,000).

day_by_day.notes: Allow ample time for check-out and airport transfer — Monday evenings can have traffic congestion. Purchase any remaining omiyage (souvenirs) at the airport's excellent duty-free shops, which stock premium Japanese whisky, matcha, and confectionery. Keep a small amount of yen for last-minute purchases as some market vendors are cash-only.
